title: SDK contract for iterator-based pagination, resumable streams, and deterministic retry surface
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD defining required behaviors and acceptance criteria for SDK iterator-based pagination (sync/async generators), resumable streaming APIs, and a deterministic retry surface across Python, TypeScript, and Go clients. Goal: make pagination and streaming reliable for production apps while enabling safe, predictable retries and compatible upgrades.
scope: Define canonical iterator/stream primitives for each language (Python generator / async generator, TS AsyncIterable, Go channel/iterator pattern)
Specify cursor semantics and opaque resume tokens for pagination and streaming partial results
Specify retry semantics: idempotency guarantees, client-provided idempotency keys, exponential backoff with jitter defaults, and upper bounds
Document compatibility guarantees and versioning policy for SDK surface changes
Provide test plan and automated integration tests to validate resume and retry behaviors against a Redwood staging endpoint
out_of_scope: Server-side protocol changes outside the public API (handled by runtime team PRD)
Language-specific ergonomic wrappers beyond the canonical primitives (e.g., third-party helper libraries)
Long-term archival of resumed stream states (beyond resume token validity window)
requirements: REQ-1: All SDKs must expose uniform iterator primitives that allow consumers to iterate over paginated resources without manually handling offsets or page numbers.
REQ-2: SDKs must return an opaque resume_token with every page and stream fragment; resume_token must be accepted by subsequent calls to continue from the last confirmed item.
REQ-3: Streaming APIs must allow resumable reads: on transient disconnects the client should be able to resume with the last resume_token and not re-receive already-delivered items.
REQ-4: Retry surface must be deterministic: retries for non-idempotent operations require an idempotency_key parameter; SDKs must surface helper generation utilities.
REQ-5: Default retry policy: exponential backoff with full jitter, initial_delay=200ms, max_delay=5s, max_attempts=5, with hooks to override per-call and per-client.
REQ-6: Backpressure: streaming clients should provide a pull-mode and a push-mode API where applicable; the pull-mode must not buffer more than N items (configurable, default 64).

REQ-7: Clear upgrade and deprecation policy: patch releases (x.y.z) cannot change iterator semantics; minor releases (x.y) may add optional features behind flags; major releases may break behaviors with documented migration steps.
REQ-8: SDKs must emit structured telemetry events for pagination start/stop, resume events, retry attempts, and permanent failures (configurable privacy/PII-safe).
REQ-9: Provide migration guide snippets for Python, TS, and Go demonstrating common upgrade and resume scenarios.
REQ-10: Acceptance tests in CI must include chaos scenarios (mid-stream disconnect, partial page loss, clock skew) against the Redwood test harness.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Given a paginated list of 10,000 items returned in pages of 100, the SDK iterator must yield exactly 10,000 items in order when pages succeed without failures.
AC-2: Simulated transient TCP disconnect after item 237 must allow a resumed iterator using the latest resume_token to continue at item 238 with no duplicates or gaps.
AC-3: For a non-idempotent write operation, the SDK must refuse to automatically retry without an explicit idempotency_key and must provide a clear error or guidance when auto-retry is attempted.
AC-4: Default retry settings should be applied for network and 5xx errors; tests that cause 503 responses should show no more than 5 attempts and respect jitter intervals between attempts.
AC-5: TS, Python, and Go SDKs must pass language-specific integration suites demonstrating the same logical behavior (iterator ordering, resume correctness, retry determinism).
AC-6: Telemetry events for resume and retry must be emitted and visible in staging telemetry dashboard for at least one test run per CI cycle.

AC-7: Backcompat check: installing new minor SDK release in-place must not change existing iterator semantics for applications not opting into new flags; CI must run backwards-compat regression tests.
migration_guide: Provide step-by-step examples: 1) Add resume_token handling pattern for long-running consumers; 2) Add idempotency_key to non-idempotent calls and switch retries to conditional retry helpers; 3) If upgrading major version, follow API mapping table in compatibility_matrix and enable feature flags in staging before production.
compatibility_matrix: sdk-2025.10 (patch) -> guarantees: iterator semantics unchanged; adds telemetry only
sdk-2026.03 (minor) -> guarantees: new optional resume_token format available behind flag; backwards-compatible parser provided
sdk-2027.0 (major) -> may change default buffering semantics; migration required: call set_buffer_limit() or retain old behavior via compatibility_mode flag
risks: R1: Resume token format changes could break long-lived consumers — mitigate with versioned token header and dual-parsing support.
R2: Incorrect client-side buffering could cause OOM in memory-constrained environments — mitigate with conservative defaults and explicit limits.
R3: Inconsistent retry semantics across languages could lead to duplicate side-effects — mitigate with shared spec tests and idempotency_key enforcement.
R4: Telemetry volume may increase unexpectedly when resume/retry loops occur — mitigate by sampling and configurable telemetry levels.
qa_notes: Include fuzzing tests that drop random chunks of stream and assert resume correctness.
Add unit tests for helper idempotency_key generators and ensure deterministic output for seeded RNG.
Run integration tests with fault-injection proxy (tc/netem) to simulate latency and packet loss patterns.
